glosses: An infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae, gradually producing nerve damage and patches of skin necrosis and historically handled by permanently quarantining its sufferers.

examples.text: Leprosy seems to have spread from India to the Middle East by early antiquity and from there to Europe during the time of the Roman Empire.
Then is it surely a leprosy
The great London doctors knew nothing about leprosy and cared less.
The new drug—diaminodiphenylsulphone... offers the first certain cure... and leprosy can be cured in six months

glosses: Similar contagious skin diseases causing light patches of scaly skin, particularly psoriasis, syphilis, vitiligo, scabies, and (biblical) the various diseases considered \"tzaraath\" in the Old Testament.
Anything considered similarly permanent, harmful, and communicable, particularly when such a thing should be handled by avoidance or isolation of its victims.

examples.text: Sin is a spiritual leprosy.

glosses: A contagious disease causing similar effects in animals, particularly
Ellipsis of murine leprosy or feline leprosy (“diseases caused in rodents and cats by Mycobacterium lepraemurium”).
A contagious disease causing similar effects in animals, particularly
Synonym of mange and glanders in horses.
Synonym of leprosarium: a place for the housing of lepers in isolation from the rest of society.
